codexExecution: Separately pinned CLI; matched model/reasoning/single-agent controls, not the Vector product revision
costBasis: Usage-derived actual funded-meter receipts, not invoice-reconciled

decision.qualityPriority: No lower quality on any task; a stronger task cannot offset a weaker task. Cost is secondary.
decision.qualityScope: Only the measured functional gates and fixed blinded source/screenshot rubric. Different material risks and unobserved behavior remain; this is not production quality assurance.
decision.conclusion: The candidate meets the bounded measured per-task quality gate but saves 5.01218433% aggregate cost, below 20%. The cost target is unmet; neither general cheapness nor a general quality or release guarantee is established.

outboxAuditAndContinuation.continuation: Only the missing Codex arm ran under the immutable pre-Vector plan and unchanged task/execution pins; no rerun, refund or repair.
outboxAuditAndContinuation.independentImagesPerRuntime: Two 390px queued/delivered end states; no independent desktop view

materialLimits.workflow: Both default data discovery and conditional process/persistence cleanup risks; Vector native empty-form alert gap, Codex small/low-contrast metadata.
materialLimits.evidence: Codex large scalar-array allocation risk; Vector direct-handler/store-only authored lifecycle coverage.
materialLimits.outbox: Vector unbounded backlog concurrency; Codex legacy failed-row recovery and open-editor queue/cancel gaps.
materialLimits.review: Static exact source plus selected independent screenshots; reviewers did not execute apps or authored tests.

accountingCheckpoint.scope: Historical study checkpoint at the three-task stage settlement

interpretationLimits: Two development replications and one held-out task in a small adaptive study are not independent broad statistical evidence.
No statistical significance, universal cost reduction, general production quality guarantee, multi-specialist/judge behavior or billions-of-tokens quality claim is established.
Score totals 139 versus 138 are descriptive only; the quality gate was checked on every task independently and cannot average away a weaker task.
Outbox manual dispositions are bounded posthoc reviews; source hashes authenticate current support copies, not historical executed bytes.
